analytic.title: Enhancing Schedulability: A Real-Time Object Slicing Approach

application.desc: GROBID - A machine learning software for extracting information from scholarly documents

div.head: In the real-time systems, designers typically focus on designing a functionally correct system. They later test it for its timing performance. Therefore, errors due to overloaded resources are exposed very late in the development process, and often at run-time. In this case, there will be many fine tunings and rewrites, making the system increasingly more dij7cult to understand, maintain, and extend. Indeed, in the object-oriented model, developers must retrieve and understand the object interdependency timing behavior, to analyze and rearrange the code. In order to help achieve schedulability, we propose an alternative to this painful process, which extends previous solutions, to deal with the real-time object model. We apply the concept of dependency analysis to the object-oriented model of the real-time task, that we restructure in a way to enhance the global schedulability.
Introduction
div.p: The domain we consider is that of the real-time applications, where tasks are regularly performed to control physical processes and monitor functioning. Meeting the timing constraints is extremely important in such systems. A task that overruns may lead to missed deadline and failure of the whole system [4]. But, errors due to overloaded resources are exposed very late in a development process, and often at run-time [5]. Specifically, any deadline violation makes tasks unschedulable. In this case, achieving schedulability is usually handled by brute-force, and manual techniques.

On the other hand, the object-oriented model features such as inheritance and polymorphism provide a great benefit in reusability and flexibility, but they make more difficult such a painful and costly process. Developers must retrieve and understand the object interdependency timing behavior, in order to analyze and rearrange its internal code.

There are some works, which partially treated such problems, such as those in [5, 1 I], but they are restrained to procedural and monolithic programs with simple realtime constructs, albeit they gave an important solution regarding the schedulability improvement.

In order to help achieve schedulability, we propose a semi-automatic approach that extends previous solutions to deal with the real-time object model. Specifically, when a set of tasks is found to be overloaded and not schedulable, a scheduling analyzer selects appropriate tasks to be restructured. We built the restructuring module by applying the concept of dependency analysis to the obj ect-oriented system. Thus, our restructuring approach is based on two concepts: program slicing and the fixed priority scheduling technique. Program slicing, first defined by Weiser [17], is based on static dataflow analysis on the flow graph of the program. It is a technique for isolating computational threads in programs. A program slice consists of the parts of a program that potentially affect the values computed at some point of interest. Such a point of interest, a slicing point of interest, is often specified by a location in the program in combination with a subset of a program's variable. For example, we can isolate a slice with regard to a critical-instruction or method call in the program, an instruction that emits command to an actuator or an instruction of an alarm in a control task.

By using the program slicing, our restructuring method allows to improve the schedulability of a task set in two ways. First, while respecting the different dependencies in the code of an unschedulable task, we ensure so that statements that influence the deadline (temporal fragment) are executed in the first place. The code fragment that corresponds to a local computation (non-temporal fiagment) can be deferred. Second, it allows decomposing a task or more into subtasks, so that we can use a generalized futed-priority scheduling methods [7], that can increase the schedulability of a task set, over that provided by the simple rate-monotonic algorithm [12,161. By restructuring a selected task among the original task set, we can enhance the overall schedulability.

In the article remainder, we present in section 2 the real-time task model on which we will apply our restructuring process. Section 3 describes the representation of different object-oriented concepts, with some adaptations to deal with our restructuring process that is described in Section 4. Finally, conclusion is presented in section 5.

div.head: Real-Time Task Model
div.p: The computation uniformity model of the objectoriented paradigm allows good real-time entities representation, either that is physical or software [2]. For example, in the manipulator control software, software objects represent the manipulator itself, the actuators, and the conceptual entities for the planner. The Java real-time object model [3] offers constructs that allow developer to tailor the implementations of specific objects and messages to gain acceptable efficiency and predictability A periodic task, denoted by 7, is an infinite sequence of task instances requested at a fixed rate in a real-time environment.

div.head: Scheduling Approaches
div.p: The most fundamental and classical problem in realtime systems is the scheduling of set of periodic tasks, to execute on a single CPU [5]. This model can be described by: (1) a task is a single-threaded program (timing block), which executes with positive periodicity and never terminates, where this type of program is the most common building block found in real-time applications, and (2) a task set is a collection of periodic tasks.

Consider a set of n periodic tasks T~,z~,. . ., q. Each task is characterized by three components: (C, Ti, Di), K i l n . A real-time scheduler [12] decides when each task gets the processor. A theoretical treatment of fixed-priority scheduling first appeared in 1973, when Liu and Layland [ 161 introduced the rate monotonic algorithm for independent periodic tasks. Harbour et al. [7] have considered a more general class of problems, and provided a framework to perform a schedulability analysis in the context of fixed-priority scheduling algorithm of tasks composed of subtasks, that have different priority levels. Compared to the rate-monotonic technique, it has been showed that this method provides a better schedulability .

div.head: Task Restructuring
div.p: In order to obtain flexible deadlines of tasks, because the schedulability is improved as one increases the flexibility of deadlines, we make a transformation on the program task such that we allow a task to go beyond of its deadline. We can get this advantage by displacing the non-temporal fragment to execute after the temporal one. Then, fragments will be sequentially recomposed, to constitute a new program of the task in question, which is semantically equivalent to the original task program.

On the other hand, we offer a mean to extract subtasks from a task in order to apply the scheduling framework developed in [7], where it has been shown that such a framework provides a better schedulability, compared to the rate-monotonic technique.

div.head: Dependency Representation
div.p: An efficient graph representation for object-oriented software should consist of a class representation that can be reused in the construction of other classes and applications that use the class. A representation must account for the dependencies of instances variables between calls to object's methods by a calling program even though the instance variables are not visible to the calling program [2,9, 101.

To do this, we build an Extended System Dependence Graph (ESDG), based on the representation of the different object-oriented concepts, mainly those proposed in [12,14,151, with some adaptations that we introduce, and that are n e c e s s q to our restructuring process.

div.head: Conclusion
div.p: In this paper, we presented an extended approach to improve the real-time application schedulability. It is based on two concepts: the object slicing, and the fixedpriority scheduling theory. Thus, we showed that we could increase the fixed-priority schedulability of a task set by two ways: first, we decompose the program of an unschedulable task into two fragments, then we splice the non-temporal fragment at the end of the temporal one.

Second, by decomposing one or more of the tasks into subtasks that are executed at modified priority levels, we can increase the overall schedulability over that provided by the simple rate-monotonic scheduling algorithm.

Therefore, applied to the real-time object-oriented programs, the complementary nature of our restructuring approach to a schedulability analysis tool will be a base of tools that enhance timing predictability without sacrificing good engineering practices. These two techniques used such a way constitute a part of an overall real-time software development process.

. To focus on the real-time system, we have treated in this article, constructs that are more used in real-time programming languages. Currently, we are implementing a prototype based on our restructuring techniques, for real-time java language [3], to experiment with useful applications in the real-time domain.
